title: ChronologyEvent
description: A single dated event in a matter's chronology - see skills/legal-evidence/SKILL.md. Added after an operational review found chronology was described only in prose with no structured record, so two sessions building the same matter's timeline had no common format to reconcile against.

event_id.description: Stable ID, e.g. CHR-001 - see docs/ID_CONVENTIONS.md

date.description: ISO date, if known at all. Not required - an event whose date is genuinely unknown is still a real chronology entry (the gap itself can be legally significant, e.g. an undated protected disclosure or an undated decision letter) and must not be left unrecorded just because it has no date yet. Omit this field entirely rather than guessing a date; set date_certainty to UNKNOWN instead.

date_certainty.description: Required even when date is present, so a reader always knows how much to trust it. UNKNOWN with no date field is valid and expected for an event whose timing is not yet established.

time.description: ISO time, if known and material

fact_ids.description: Cross-reference to fact.schema.json records - a chronology event and the facts it supports should share IDs, not drift independently
